name: What B144 should be stocked with, and what nobody has counted
description: the consumables with their target and reorder threshold, their vendor and on-campus source — and the fact that no stock level has ever been recorded for any of them, so nothing here says what is actually low
phrases: what do we need to reorder
what is the target stock for that
returns: the counts: how many locations carry a target, how many do not, how many hold more than one item. --json adds every location with its items, target, threshold, vendor_url, campus_source and preferred_acquire.

requires.note: target and threshold per row — what SHOULD be there. There is no column for what IS there, which is why this verb cannot report what is low.

notes: IT REPORTS THAT NOBODY HAS LOOKED, NOT THAT NOTHING IS NEEDED. consumables.tsv has no column for the amount on the shelf; that number would come from the steward count sheets, and as of 2026-10-15 not one has ever been submitted across eight steward folders. An item with a target and no count is UNMEASURED, and printing a short 'nothing to reorder' list would be the most dangerous possible output because it reads as a checked room. SECOND FINDING, REPORTED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED: target and threshold are recorded per ROW while the map is keyed by LOCATION, so where two items share a location the last row's target is the one that survives and may describe a different item. 3 of 70 locations are like that.
